overview.title: A medina you can learn without getting lost for hours
overview.p1: The medina of Meknes is smaller and more navigable than Fez el-Bali, which makes it ideal if you want souks, workshops and neighbourhood life without the full labyrinth. Lanes open toward Place el-Hedim; others lead deeper into food stalls, textiles and everyday shops.
overview.p2: You will still get turned around once or twice — that is normal. Use the main square as your reset point. The pleasure here is ordinary commerce: olives, spices, metalwork, and doors that open onto quiet courtyards.
overview.p3: Morning is best for cooler air and active markets. Keep afternoons shorter in summer. Dar Jamai Museum sits on the edge and pairs well with a medina loop.

q1.question: Is the medina easy to navigate?
q1.answer: Easier than Fez, but still a maze in places. Note landmarks and return to Place el-Hedim when unsure.

q2.question: Do I need a guide?
q2.answer: Not required for a first look. A guide helps if you want workshops and history without wrong turns.

q3.question: Is bargaining expected?
q3.answer: For crafts and many market goods, yes — stay polite and be ready to walk away.

q4.question: Is it open in the evening?
q4.answer: Main lanes stay active into the evening; some shops close earlier. The square remains the safest orientation point after dark.

q5.question: What should I buy?
q5.answer: Olives, local food products and small crafts. For carpets and high-value pieces, take time and compare.

food.title: Eat in the lanes
food.p1: Medina grills and small kitchens are the point: skewers, bread, soups and olives. Follow busy local tables rather than empty tourist fronts.
food.p2: For a longer meal, riad restaurants offer courtyard seating a few minutes from the main souks.
food.li2: Olives and spices as edible souvenirs
food.li3: Simple soup or stew at midday
food.li4: Tea when you need a pause from bargaining
food.li5: Avoid the emptiest “menu touristique” boards if the room is silent

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting the Meknes Medina

1.title: Reset on Place el-Hedim
1.desc: When the lanes confuse you, walk back to the square instead of accepting the first “shortcut” offer. Most helpful directions start from Hedim anyway.

2.title: Shop with patience
2.desc: Calmer than Fez does not mean no pressure. Smile, compare two or three stalls, and treat bargaining as conversation rather than combat.

3.title: Combine with Dar Jamai
3.desc: The museum gives context to the crafts you see in the souks. Doing both the same half-day links objects in glass cases with the living market outside.
